title: Pluggable checkpoint adapter and tokenizer handoff simplification
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: The current model loading pipeline has grown organic complexity across multiple adapters (legacy checkpoint loader, v2 shard reader, on-disk/remote format handlers) and an ad-hoc tokenizer handoff path. This causes duplicated weight mapping logic, inconsistent shard manifests, and two separate code paths that transform tokenizer vocab/merges into runtime tokenizers. Consequences: long model onboarding times, frequent regressions when adding quantized formats, and runtime memory spikes during loading.

Goal: Replace brittle format-specific code with a pluggable checkpoint adapter interface, consolidate shard/manifest handling, and extract a small tokenizer-handoff contract ("vocab bridge") used by both the loader and the serving runtime. The work should be backwards-compatible: existing model bundles and manifests continue to load while new adapters are introduced behind feature flags.

Approach summary:
- Define CheckpointAdapter V1 interface (open_file, stream_weights, metadata, shard_manifest) and minimal shim for legacy loaders.
- Implement two adapters: legacy-shard-shim and unified-manifest-reader. The unified adapter understands canonical manifest fields (shard_uuid, byte_range, hash) and negotiates preferred transfer (http-range vs s3 multipart).
- Introduce TokenizerHandoff API: a compact JSON contract (vocab_path, merges_path, special_tokens_map, tokenizer_version) and a runtime converter that produces the runtime Tokenizer object lazily (deferred load during first inference to reduce peak memory during bulk model loads).
- Add migration tooling to generate canonical manifests for existing bundles and CI check to validate adapter parity.
- Add performance microbenchmarks to measure model load latency, peak RSS, and disk throughput before/after.

Non-goals: changing on-disk bundle formats in this sprint, full replacement of quantized kernels, or changing runtime KV cache semantics.
acceptance_criteria: CheckpointAdapter interface defined and documented in code and Confluence
Legacy loader functionally shimmed to the new adapter with feature-flag toggle
TokenizerHandoff JSON contract implemented and both loader and serving runtime can consume it lazily
Migration tool can convert 95% of existing customer bundles to canonical manifests (edge cases logged)
Benchmarks show <=10% load latency regression and peak RSS reduced by at least 15% for multi-model batch loads
Unit and integration tests covering adapter selection, manifest verification, and tokenizer handoff
updates: 2026-02-18 - Created ticket. Initial spike done: evaluated three approaches (adapter interface, monolithic loader rewrite, and middleware shim). Chose adapter interface to minimize risk.
